transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-05
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM - partial), Ben Owens (CTO), Dana Park (Head of Security), Miguel Santos (Lead Platform Eng), Tara Liu (Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, terse):
SkylineWare is evaluating Redwood for inference hosting. Key concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, RBAC granularity, audit log access/retention, data residency and retention/deletion guarantees. Redwood AE/SE walked through hosting options and high-level mitigations. Agreed next steps: send SOC2 report, SAML/SCIM guide, schedule technical deep dive.

Topics:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2 Type II, ISO-27001 question)
- Authn/authz: SSO (SAML/OKTA), SCIM, RBAC roles
- Encryption: at rest, in-transit, CMK/HSM options (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault), customer-managed keys
- Audit logs, retention windows, retention export
- Deployment choices: Hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private VPC/on-prem
- Data deletion, retention policy, legal holds

Action items (captured briefly): see action_items meta above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for making time, um, we'll do a quick intros then jump to the security questions. Ben, you said you'd only be here for first ten?
[00:05] Ben Owens: Yeah sorry, back-to-back. I'll hang for the intro and then hand off to Dana and Miguel.
[00:09] Dana Park: Hi all. We're trying to understand if Redwood's hosted offering can meet our compliance needs or whether we need dedicated or private. SOC2 is table-stakes but we also have some ISO-reqs and data residency for EU customers.
[00:18] Alex Chen: Totally, that's a common mode. Quick overview: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Hosted is fastest, Dedicated gives isolation and reserved throughput, Private gives full control incl. customer-managed networking and optional on-prem. We'll focus on controls and artifacts.
[00:32] Priya Rao: hi, and on the infra side I can speak to the key management and audit logs, and we can walk through SCIM/SAML.
[00:39] Miguel Santos: Great, high level first: are we able to bring our own keys? We need CMKs, ideally HSM-backed, and we can't have Redwood rotate the keys without our approval.
[00:46] Priya Rao: short answer: yes for Private; for Dedicated and Hosted we have options. Hosted supports envelope encryption with a customer-managed KMS in certain enterprise plans — you can provide a customer CMK in AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault, and we store ciphertext; we don't have plaintext keys. There's also bring-your-own-HSM for Private. Note: hosted CMK support requires contract addendum and is in the higher-tier enterprise plan.
[01:10] Dana Park: ok is that HSM-backed? We need attestations that the key material is in an HSM with FIPS 140-2 level 3 ideally.
[01:16] Priya Rao: on Private you can use your own HSM; for customer-managed KMS on hosted we rely on the cloud provider's HSM (AWS KMS uses HSMs, FIPS 140-2 certified) — we can provide the cert chain in the attestation packet.
[01:29] Tara Liu: on legal side, what's the retention / deletion guarantee? We have customers with 7 year retention on some PII, but we also need to be able to purge for data subject requests.
[01:37] Alex Chen: Good point. Our default retention for user-level logs is 90 days, audit logs 365 days by default, but we can adjust retention windows on Dedicated/Private. Deletion: we expose APIs to delete data; on Private you control persistent storage so you can implement your own deletion flow. For Hosted we support deletion requests and will confirm deletion within SLA, and we provide certification that data was purged. Caveat: backups has a separate retention cycle, we can include those in the deletion process per contract.
[02:05] Miguel Santos: backups — are they encrypted with the same CMK or a Redwood-managed key?
[02:09] Priya Rao: backups in Hosted are encrypted with your CMK when CMK support is enabled; otherwise Redwood-managed keys. On Dedicated, we can configure per-pool encryption settings.
[02:18] Ben Owens: Can we export audit logs and ship them to our SIEM (we use Splunk)? We want a copy of every inference request/response meta for forensic purposes (not outputs necessarily), and retention in our own account.
[02:27] Priya Rao: yes — we provide streaming audit logs to customer-owned destinations: S3, Event Hubs, or direct SIEM connectors. For Hosted that streaming is via a secure push to your account; for Dedicated/Private it's simpler since it's inside your environment. We can include request metadata, route info, latency, error codes, and access logs. Note there's PII considerations so you might exclude user content bodies.
[02:47] Dana Park: Request/response metadata — we need to know which fields are included by default. Also, can we redact request content before it hits logs?
[02:53] Priya Rao: default audit entries include request id, model id, timestamp, token count, route, and non-sensitive headers. Content bodies are logged only if you opt-in for debugging. You can enable content-masking or client-side hashing before sending. We'll send the audit log schema in the follow-up.
[03:12] Alex Chen: quick question from our side: do you have an existing SSO provider? You mentioned Okta earlier?
[03:16] Miguel Santos: yes, Okta. We also leverage SCIM to provision groups.
[03:19] Alex Chen: we support SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning, SSO metadata import, and role mappings. SCIM can sync groups so you can map Okta groups to Redwood RBAC roles. We also support OIDC for some setups.
[03:31] Dana Park: RBAC granularity — we need separation between platform engineers, data scientists, and product support. Also an audit trail of admin-level actions (who triggered model swaps, rollouts, or exported logs).
[03:42] Priya Rao: our RBAC supports role types: viewer, developer, admin, ops, and custom roles on Dedicated/Private. All admin actions are logged in the audit trail. For Hosted we have predefined roles and scoped-API tokens; for Dedicated we can enable fine-grained custom roles.
[03:58] Tara Liu: For regulatory purposes we need to know if Redwood personnel ever access production keys or data. Is there an operator break-glass?
[04:06] Alex Chen: Redwood's standard is zero access to plaintext model inputs/outputs for Hosted when CMK enabled and encryption at rest/in transit applied. For Dedicated we provide the control plane; operator access is limited and, when needed for support, requires customer approval and is time-limited, logged, and can be constrained via Just-in-Time access with recorded sessions. We can add a stipulation in the SLA that Redwood cannot decrypt content without an explicit signed request.
[04:28] Miguel Santos: ok that aligns. Next: SOC2. Can you share Type II and the period? Also ISO?
[04:34] Alex Chen: We have SOC2 Type II covering common criteria; the latest report covers the period Jan–Dec 2027. We also have ISO 27001 scope for the inference platform — I'll attach those documents. For legal/insurance we also provide penetration testing summary and vulnerability management cadence.
[04:48] Ben Owens: If we go hosted, is there a way to geofence data to EU? We have EU customers and can't cross certain data boundaries.
[04:55] Priya Rao: we have region-aware routing. Hosted can pin workloads to specific regions, and we can store logs and artifacts in region-specific buckets. For strict geofencing Private/VPC is best since you control the environment.
[05:06] Dana Park: timeline — our procurement and security sign-offs need artifacts in two weeks if we're going to start a pilot in August. Is that feasible?
[05:12] Alex Chen: yes, sending the SOC2 and SAML docs today, and Priya will follow with a technical deck and sample config. We can do a short pilot on Dedicated within a couple weeks once contracts are agreed.
[05:22] Miguel Santos: about performance benchmarking — if we're doing a POC we want reproducible latency and cost numbers. Do you have a benchmark harness or a spreadsheet?
[05:30] Priya Rao: we have a perf harness and can run a dedicated benchmark in your environment, or run a Redwood-hosted benchmark with comparable hardware. We'll share a template spreadsheet and can run a joint benchmark during the POC.
[05:40] Tara Liu: any data processing addendum templates? We'd need a DPA with EU clauses.
[05:44] Alex Chen: yes we have a DPA template and standard DPAs including EU addenda; we'll attach that.
[05:49] Ben Owens: Can you explain the fallback policy? If a region has an outage, does traffic route to another region and how does that affect residency?
[05:57] Priya Rao: fallback is policy-driven. You can set strict residency (no fallback) or set cost/latency-driven fallback where the system will route to the nearest compatible region. For strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated pinned to region.
[06:10] Dana Park: about logs retention, you mentioned 365 days by default — what's archival vs live? And are logs immutable?
[06:16] Priya Rao: live logs are stored in a write-once object store with versioning turned on; immutability/retention holds are configurable for Dedicated/Private. Archival to cold storage is available and we can set lifecycle policies to move to Glacier/Archive.
[06:29] Miguel Santos: does Redwood support long-term retention for legal holds? We might need to retain some sets for up to 7+ years.
[06:34] Alex Chen: yes — through contractual addendum we can support extended legal retention; cost implications apply and we'd set up export/archival to your owned buckets for longer retention to avoid vendor lock.
[06:45] Ben Owens: does Redwood maintain a vulnerability disclosure program and do you produce SOC penetration test reports for customers?
[06:52] Priya Rao: we do — vulnerability disclosure program with a coordinated response. Pen tests are done annually; summary reports are shareable and full reports under NDA.
[07:00] Dana Park: Question: in Hosted, who owns the underlying logs for telemetry? Is Redwood the custodian and do you allow egress?
[07:07] Priya Rao: we are the initial custodian but you can configure streaming so logs copy to your cloud account (S3) in near real-time. You retain the copy; Redwood retains an operational copy for N days per policy. Both can be configured.
[07:22] Alex Chen: quick aside — pricing delta for CMK, dedicated, private is non-trivial. We'll include a pricing sketch in follow-up.
[07:28] Ben Owens: understood. Another technical: model artifact lifecycle — we want to pin model versions and roll back quickly if a model regresses. How do rollouts look and who can trigger them?
[07:36] Priya Rao: Rollouts can be canary or full. Rollouts are triggered by ops/admin roles. We support pinned model versions in the route config; audit logs capture who initiated a rollout and we have automatic fallback policies if latency or error rate increases.
[07:51] Miguel Santos: do those rollouts require infra changes?
[07:54] Priya Rao: not for model swaps — they're config operations. If you change model size or instance type on Dedicated you might need capacity changes.
[08:02] Tara Liu: legal quick Q: do you have data processing subprocessors list? We need that for our vendor assessment.
[08:08] Alex Chen: yes, subprocessors list is maintained; we'll send the latest.
[08:12] Ben Owens: ok we're about to run out of time. I'll drop off now — thanks all.
[08:16] Ben Owens: (disconnect)
[08:18] Dana Park: two quick specifics: can we get an example SAML metadata file and the minimum RBAC role matrix? Also can you confirm SCIM group sync attributes?
[08:27] Priya Rao: yes to all — we'll send a sample metadata XML, a recommended RBAC matrix for platform/data/product personas, and SCIM attribute mapping (groups, emails, displayName).
[08:36] Miguel Santos: also please include the audit log schema and an example export to Splunk — we want to validate we can map fields easily.
[08:44] Alex Chen: will do. Final note: if you want zero Redwood access to keys, Private with on-prem keystore is the way; if you want easier onboarding, Hosted with CMK or Dedicated with customer KMS is middleground.
[08:58] Dana Park: thanks. We'll review materials and aim to get back in a week with the core list and preferred pilot path.
[09:05] Tara Liu: thanks everyone, appreciate it.

Questions (spoken or typed):
- Does Redwood support customer-managed keys for backups? (answered)
- Can Redwood stream audit logs to customer SIEM? (answered)
- Is SOC2 Type II and ISO certificate available? (answered)

End of transcript.
